items.title: R-GroundBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for R-Group Groundingin Markush Molecular Editing
items.one_liner: R-GroundBench exposes severe grounding and reasoning limitations in AI models attempting complex Markush molecular editing.
items.summary: Reasoning over incomplete chemical representations like Markush structures remains a challenge for AI-driven scientific discovery, as variable R-group placeholders require grounding across multiple modalities. To address the lack of specialized evaluation, researchers introduce R-GroundBench, a diagnostic benchmark featuring a Multiple-Choice VQA track and an open-ended generation track built from real patent data. Experimental results reveal a large performance drop when moving from easy tasks to hard VQA tasks, and generation exact match remains below 20% for most models. These findings show that current AI systems still lack reliable grounding and execution capabilities for complex molecular editing.
items.bottom_line: Current vision-language and language models lack reliable R-group grounding for chemical representations, exposing major reliability gaps in AI-driven drug discovery.

items.title: MOMAT: Mixture of Multiple Atlases for Low-Power Jailbreak Defense of Quantized LLMs
items.one_liner: MOMAT secures edge-deployed quantized LLMs against jailbreaks with massive speedups using Compute-in-Memory acceleration.
items.summary: Quantized large language models deployed on edge devices are highly vulnerable to jailbreak attacks because quantization weakens their alignment safeguards. To fix this without heavy computational overhead, researchers introduce MOMAT, a hardware-enhanced safety framework combining structured knowledge retrieval with low-power Compute-in-Memory acceleration. MOMAT maps semantic clusters into multiple atlases and uses a lightweight Mixture of Experts detector to guard prompts efficiently. Evaluations show that MOMAT accelerates retrieval by millions of times and drastically cuts energy consumption while matching state-of-the-art defense performance.
key_facts: Energy reduction: ~2.5 x 10^5 times over DRAM baseline
items.bottom_line: Hardware-accelerated Compute-in-Memory retrieval can make edge-deployed quantized LLMs both robust against jailbreaks and highly energy-efficient.

items.title: PG-SFT: Balancing Capability Acquisition and Retention in Offline Agent Fine-Tuning
items.one_liner: Privilege-Guided SFT (PG-SFT) helps maintain base model reasoning capabilities while fine-tuning agents for specialized tool-use tasks.
items.summary: Researchers have developed Privilege-Guided SFT (PG-SFT) to address the capability degradation that often occurs when fine-tuning tool-using agents. By using turn-level information gain to adjust supervision strength, PG-SFT better balances the acquisition of new skills with the retention of base model capabilities. This approach reduces distributional drift compared to standard supervised fine-tuning methods.
items.bottom_line: Developers can use PG-SFT to improve agent performance on target tasks without sacrificing the model's general reasoning and code generation abilities.
